requirement:
Each prose paragraph has an anonymous `paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Heading text and literal
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes.
rationale:
I judged the three marked tests in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs` adequate for `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.paragraphs`. I worked from the test text alone and did not read any implementation source.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**
- **Anonymous `paragraph` node under the nearest enclosing container.**
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` asserts the full `kinds` outline. A top-level paragraph has the section as parent. The paragraph inside the `note` directive has that block as parent. The paragraph inside the nested `tip` directive has the inner block as parent. Line ranges are asserted too.
  - The same test checks that each paragraph's segment starts with `paragraph@` and is `kind.len() + 1 + 12` long, which covers the anonymous `kind@<12 hex>` form.
- **Paragraphs before the first heading, in list items, and in quotations.** `paragraphs_in_transparent_lists_and_quotes_are_selectable` uses a document that starts with "Before heading.", then a list item paragraph and a quoted paragraph. It asserts four paragraphs at lines `[1, 3, 5, 10]`. It asserts the first three have the enclosing section (node 1) as parent. It asserts the paragraph after the setext heading has `section[Title]` as parent.
- **Paragraphs in directive bodies.** The first test covers this for both nested directive levels.
- **Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.**
  - The first test checks that `outline.resolve(&node.selector)` returns each node's index.
  - `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` covers the rest. Selectors are stable under reflow. Selectors are stable when sibling content is edited. Duplicate sibling paragraphs get `#1` and `#2`. The test applies the same `#N` check to duplicate blocks.
- **Heading text creates no paragraph nodes.** The ATX heading `# Authentication` in the first test and the setext heading `Title\n=====` in the second test produce no paragraph nodes. The exact node-list assertion in the first test and the paragraph count of 4 in the second would fail if either did.
- **Literal code-block contents create no paragraph nodes.** The first test's fenced `text` block containing `hi` yields only a `block` node. The exact node-list equality rules out an extra paragraph.

**Gaps**
I found no uncovered obligation and no weak assertion. The tests do not cover a list or quote nested inside a directive, or several paragraphs in one list item. The requirement does not name those cases, so I did not count them as gaps. There are no acknowledgments, and none are needed.

text: Each prose paragraph has an anonymous `paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes.
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
